text: The correct order of reactivity of the given chlorides with acetate in acetic acid is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Acetate in acetic acid is a weak nucleophile in a polar protic, ionising solvent, so these chlorides react by the $S_{N}1$ path; the rate follows the stability of the carbocation formed on loss of $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$.

3-Chloro-1-methylcyclohexene gives an allylic cation whose positive charge is shared between a secondary carbon and the methyl-bearing tertiary carbon, the most stable cation of the four.

3-Chloro-4-methylcyclohexene gives an allylic cation shared between two secondary carbons; the methyl on the neighbouring $sp^{3}$ carbon adds only weak $+I$ and hyperconjugative help, less than placing the charge on a tertiary carbon, so it comes second.

5-Chloro-3-methylcyclohexene has Cl on a carbon not adjacent to the C=C, so it gives an ordinary secondary carbocation without allylic stabilisation.

3-(Chloromethyl)cyclohexene would have to form a primary carbocation, the least stable, so it reacts slowest.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift

text:
Consider the following cell reaction :

$Cd_{(s)}+Hg_{2}SO_{4(s)}+\frac{9}{5}H_{2}O_{(l)}$ $⇌$ $CdSO_{4}.\frac{9}{5}H_{2}O_{(s)}+2Hg_{(l)}$

The value of $E_{cell}^{0}$ is 4.315 V at 25${}^{\circ }$C. If $\Delta$H${}^{\circ }$ = $-$825.2 kJ mol$^{-1}$, the standard entropy change $\Delta$S${}^{\circ }$ in $J K^{-1}$ is $___________. ($Nearest integer) [Given : Faraday constant = 96487 C mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta G^{\circ }=-nFE^{\circ }=\Delta H^{\circ }-T\Delta S^{\circ }$

$\therefore$ $\Delta$S${}^{\circ }$ $=\frac{\Delta H^{\circ }+nFE^{\circ }}{T}$

$=\frac{(-825.2\times 10^{3})+(2\times 96487\times 4.315)}{298}$

$=\frac{-825.2\times 10^{3}+832.682\times 10^{3}}{298}$

$=\frac{7.483\times 10^{3}}{298}=25.11$ $JK^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$

$\therefore$ Nearest integer answer is 25.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift

text:
The total number of reagents from those given below, that can convert nitrobenzene into aniline is $___________. ($Integer answer)

I. Sn $-$ HCl

II. Sn $-$ $NH_{4}OH$

III. Fe $-$ HCl

IV. Zn $-$ HCl

$V. H_{2}$ $-$ Pd

$VI. H_{2}$ $-$ Raney Nickel
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Nitrobenzene is reduced to aniline by a metal in acid medium or by catalytic hydrogenation:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}+6[\mathrm{H}]\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$


[IMG]

Sn–HCl, Fe–HCl and Zn–HCl (I, III, IV) are metals in acid medium; they reduce $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ to $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$–Pd and $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$–Raney nickel (V, VI) reduce $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ to $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ by catalytic hydrogenation.

Sn–$\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ (II) provides no acid; tin acts as the reducing agent for this conversion only in acid medium, so it does not give aniline.

The reagents that convert nitrobenzene into aniline are I, III, IV, V and VI.

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift

text: Ge(Z = 32) in its ground state electronic configuration has x completely filled orbitals with $m_{l} = 0$. The value of x is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ground-state configuration of Ge (Z = 32): $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}4s^{2}3d^{10}4p^{2}$.

Every subshell has exactly one orbital with $m_{l}=0$. In the completely filled subshells 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s and 3d, this orbital holds 2 electrons, giving 7 such orbitals.

In $4p^{2}$, by Hund's rule the two electrons occupy two different 4p orbitals singly, so no 4p orbital is completely filled.

$x=7$

Hence, the answer is 7.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift
